nodes.name: Acid Precipitation of WO3·2H2O
nodes.procedure: 50 ml of 1M Na2WO4·2H2O (99+% Acros Organics) was added dropwise to 450 ml of 4 N HCl (Certified ACS Plus, Fisher Chemical) while stirring at 300 rpm for ~24 h. The precipitates were collected and washed with deionized water using vacuum filtration until the rinsed solution reached pH 6-7. The filtered WO3·2H2O was then dried at 60°C overnight and ground into a fine powder.

nodes.source_text: WO3·H2O was synthesized via an acid precipitation reaction.15 Briefly, 50 ml of 1M [Na2WO4·2H2O 99+% Acros Organics) was added dropwise to 450 ml of 4 N HCl ... dried at 60°C overnight and ground into a fine powder.

nodes.name: Dehydration
nodes.procedure: To obtain WO3·H2O, the WO3·2H2O powder was heated overnight at 120°C.
nodes.source_text: To obtain WO3·H2O, the WO3·2H2O powder was heated overnight at 120°C.

nodes.name: Octylamine Pillaring
nodes.procedure: WO3·H2O was added to a solution of octylamine (99+%, Acros Organics) in heptane (99%, Acros Organics) with a molar ratio of 15 OA to 1 WO3·H2O and a volume ratio of 5 heptane to 1 octylamine independent of the size of the reaction. This mixture was stirred rigorously in a roundbottom flask for six days. The reaction completion was marked by a color change from yellow to white. After completion, the powder was collected via centrifugation and washed by redispersing the powder in ethanol and centrifuging three times. The resulting material was dried at 60°C under vacuum and ground to form a fine powder.

nodes.name: Acid Exchange to exWO3·2H2O
nodes.procedure: Exchanged WO3·2H2O (exWO3·2H2O) was obtained by stirring OA–WO3 in 4M H2SO4 (Certified ACS Plus, Fisher Chemical). The sulfuric acid was refreshed daily by centrifuging the powder and redispersing in a new solution until the powder turned yellow. exWO3·2H2O was collected via the same centrifugation procedure as OA–WO3. The resulting material was dried at 60°C overnight and ground to a fine powder.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO₃·H₂O shows nanoscale platelets; OA–WO₃ shows micron-scale sheets and ribbons; exWO₃·2H₂O shows micron-scale sheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Figs. 1(d)–1(f) show the morphology of each material. WO₃·H₂O consists of nanoscale platelets typical of the acid-precipitated synthesis route.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface areas decrease in order: as-synthesized WO₃·H₂O (31.0 m²/g), OA–WO₃ (24.9 m²/g), exWO₃·2H₂O (16.4 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface area decreased in the order of as-synthesized WO₃·H₂O (31.0 m²/g), OA–WO₃ (24.9 m²/g), and exWO₃·2H₂O (16.4 m²/g).

nodes.characterization_summary: OA–WO₃ shows largest interlayer spacing of 2.6 nm; WO₃·H₂O has 0.53 nm; exWO₃·2H₂O and WO₃·2H₂O both exhibit 0.69 nm interlayer spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The OA pillars increased the interlayer spacing from 0.53 nm in WO₃·H₂O to 2.6 nm in OA–WO₃. The diffraction pattern of exWO₃·2H₂O matched that of WO₃·2H₂O... with both materials exhibiting an interlayer spacing of 0.69 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tungsten oxide hydrates display broad peak 550-750 cm⁻¹ (O-W-O stretching) and sharp peaks at ~945 cm⁻¹ (WO₃·H₂O) and ~955 cm⁻¹ (exWO₃·2H₂O) for W-Ot; OA–WO₃ shows shift to 885 cm⁻¹ plus octylamine peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The tungsten oxide hydrates display two characteristic peaks. The broad peak between 550 and 750 cm⁻¹... WO₃·H₂O and exWO₃·2H₂O contain a sharp peak at ~945 and ~955 cm⁻¹... Replacing the coordinated water... causes a shift of ν(W-Ot) to 885 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: WO₃·H₂O and exWO₃·2H₂O show ν(O-H) ~3400 cm⁻¹ and H₂O δ ~1620 cm⁻¹; OA–WO₃ shows NH₃⁺ modes (3000-3250, 2500-3000, 1606 cm⁻¹) and CH₂ modes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ν(O-H) and H₂O deformation/bending (δ) modes located at ~3400 and 1620 cm⁻¹... were observed in WO₃·H₂O and exWO₃·2H₂O. OA–WO₃ did not contain interlayer water... The presence of OA in OA–WO₃ was observed by the vibrational modes of NH₃⁺ and CH₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: All materials show W in 6+ oxidation state; WO₃·H₂O and exWO₃·2H₂O show O 1s for O-W and O-H₂ bonds; OA–WO₃ shows O 1s at 530.8 eV (O-W), N 1s at 399.7 eV (R-NH₂) and 401.6 eV (R-NH₃⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on XPS peak fitting of the W 4f₅/₂ and W 4f₇/₂ peaks, tungsten is in the 6+ oxidation state... The O 1s core spectrum indicates the presence of O-W and O-H₂ bonds... The O 1s core spectrum for OA–WO₃ shows one peak at 530.8 eV... Two peaks were present in the N 1s core spectrum.

nodes.characterization_summary: OA–WO₃ contains ~2.6 mol OA per 1 mol WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) (Fig. S3) shows that there are ~2.6 mol of OA to 1 mol of WO₃ in OA–WO₃.
